summary: Keenan W. Cox specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Cox earned an MA from McMaster University, studying under supervisor James A. Benn (attested 2014).

Kees W. Bolle (1927–2012) was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied at Leiden University (~1946–1953). He served as a fellow at the Netherlands Institute for Advanced Study and Professor Emeritus of History at UCLA (both attested 2005).

Kei Kataoka (born 1969) is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (PhD 1992–2001 under Hiroshi Marui) and National Sanskrit University (~1999–2001). His posts include Wolfson College, Oxford (1998–1999) and Kyushu University (~2007).

Keiichi Miyamoto (born 1948) works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1967–1977) under Minoru Hara, and served as associate professor (~1989–1997) and professor (~1997–2017) at Kokugakuin University.

Keiji Nishitani (1900–1990) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1921–1924) under Kitaro Nishida, and held appointments at Kyoto University (~1935–1963) and Otani University (~1963–1971).

Keiki Yabuki (1879–1939) worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying at Tohoku Fukushi, Taisho, and Tokyo universities. He founded Miwa Gakuin and taught at Shukyo University (~1913–1926), University of Tokyo (~1924–1935), and Taisho University (~1926–1939).

Keikyo Nakamikado specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Nakamikado held posts at Bukkyo University as a research collaborator (attested 2003) and at the Chion-in Institute of Jodo Sect Studies as a researcher (attested 2015).
Keir Magalie Strickland works in history, archaeology, and Indology. Strickland completed a PhD at Durham University under the supervision of Robin Coningham (attested 2011).

Keishin Okamura (1931–2019) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1950–1958). Okamura held posts at Koyasan University as an associate professor (~1967–1974) and at Kōchi University.

Keisho Tsukamoto (1929–2010) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned doctoral degrees at Tohoku University (~1953–1964). He served as professor at Tohoku University (attested 1980–2001) and president of Hosen Gakuen College (~1993–1999).

Keith Dowman (born 1945) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under traditional teachers including Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje (~1969–1987), Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche (~1971–1991), Chatral Sangye Dorje Rinpoche, and Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche.

Keiya Noguchi (born 1954) specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, completing doctoral studies at Kyoto University (~1980–1985). Noguchi held positions at Shuchiin University (attested 1995–2005) and Taisho University, including institute director (attested 2017).

Keizaburō Mizuno (1932–2026) was an art historian and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1956). Mizuno held positions at Tokyo National Museum (1958–1968), Tokyo University of the Arts (~2000), and Niigata Prefectural Museum of Modern Art (2000–2008).

Kelsey Alise Seymour specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies, completing a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Victor H. Mair (attested 2018). Seymour was a Visiting Predoctoral Fellow at the Max Planck Institute for the History of Science (2017–2018).

Kemu Jin (1912–2000) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Sinology. He held a post at Visva-Bharati University (1941–1945) and served as Professor of Sanskrit at Peking University (~1948–2000).
Kendall Marchman specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Marchman studied under Mario Poceski (attested 2009) and completed a PhD at the University of Florida in 2015.

Keng Ching specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, earning a PhD from Harvard University (attested 2009) under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil. Ching served as associate professor at National Chengchi University (attested 2013–2019).

Kengo Harimoto works in Indology. Harimoto earned a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania under Wilhelm Halbfass in 1999, and held posts at Mahidol University (attested 2020) and the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (attested 2021–2022).

Kenji Matsuo (born 1954) is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1974–1984) and held an academic post at Yamagata University (~1987–2020).

Kenji Takahashi is an Indologist who studied at Leiden University (2015–2016) under Peter Bisschop, Diwakar Acharya, and Yuko Yokochi. Takahashi held a JSPS-sponsored fellowship at the University of Naples Federico II (2019–2021).
